items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: I connect you with Big George Jones running from the Orleansdale Passer and said, he'll ride you down home.

ctx.x: He just died about a month ago, Ed Garland told us. Poissy Wright died? Wasn't it? Wasn't he the one? I don't know where he is. No, that was the bouncer. The bouncer died. Who was the big chaper? Oh, you're talking about Zach Williams. Zach Williams died about a month ago.

Flo Walker. Big Zach. Yeah. He used to be a, used to wake and move it, yeah. He bought my memories up together now. Well, all right. Poissy, what are you doing coming out the depot? I said, I'm just coming over and looking at the race. He says, well, what's the trouble? I said, well, I'll show him a telegram. He said, oh, I'm sorry. I live on San Pedro Street. He said, I'll tell you what I'm doing. I'm going, we're going to make a trip all the way to El Paso tonight at 1130. And when you get over there, I connect…
I don't know her name. That's skinny girl. Yeah. That's a much wife. Huh? Is that much married? Or a different girl? No.

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: I went to work in Stouroville with a guy named George John... With George Jones.

ctx.x: I mean, of Laplace. So when you arrived in New Orleans, that was in 1907, in other words, if you were 21 years old. Right? 1907. So what did you do when you arrived in New Orleans?

Well, I went to work in Stouroville with a guy named George John until I could get my band there. George Jones? George. George Jones. The boys' best players in the world. If the world could... You mean you were playing in the district?
Yeah. Where? At Pete Lallus. At Pete Lallus. With George Jones.
